conflicts.topic: effect of nickel on vacancy removal in FeAl
conflicts.claim_a: Schneibel [62] confirmed the increase in equilibrium vacancy concentration by the addition of nickel; nickel can cause softening in FeAl at high temperature anneals by reducing the vacancy hardening.
conflicts.claim_b: Pike et al. [64] believe that nickel does not prevent the removal of vacancies, which disagrees with Munroe's observation.

evidence.quote: The samples annealed at 700 °C showed significantly lower vacancy concentrations (Fig. 26), which they believe indicates that nickel does not prevent the removal of vacancies, which disagrees with Monroe's observation.
